description: We are a six-member team from Haldia, India, bringing together programming experience and full-stack development skills. For the astronaut health monitoring challenge, we’ll combine our strengths to design and build a practical software solution that helps astronauts track health indicators, notice potential changes, and make informed decisions during long-duration space missions.
summary: AstroVitals is a prototype dashboard for recording and reviewing crew health readings over a mission. Users can add crew profiles and enter daily measurements such as heart rate, blood oxygen, blood pressure, breathing rate, temperature, sleep, stress, exercise and fluid intake. The app checks the entered data and displays trends, status flags and an illustrative readiness score based on prototype rules. Example crew readings are synthetic demonstration data, not real astronaut medical records. We also include a fixed sample of 12 ISS environmental radiation measurements from NASA’s Open Science Data Repository RadLab. These DosTel readings show absorbed dose rate in µGy/hour and appear separately from crew health readings; they do not affect the readiness score. The prototype is not clinically validated and is not a medical diagnostic tool.
details:
AstroVitals is a prototype dashboard for recording and reviewing crew health readings over a mission. Users can add crew profiles and enter measurements such as heart rate, blood oxygen, blood pressure, breathing rate, temperature, sleep, stress, exercise and fluid intake. The app checks the entered data and displays trends, status flags and a readiness score based on prototype rules. Example crew readings are synthetic demonstration data, not real astronaut medical records.

We also included a fixed sample of 12 ISS DosTel environmental radiation measurements from NASA’s Open Science Data Repository RadLab. The measurements show absorbed dose rate in µGy/hour. They are displayed separately and do not affect the crew readiness score.

AstroVitals uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Node.js, JSON and SVG graphs. The prototype demonstrates data entry, validation and trend display. Its health rules and scores are not clinically validated, so it is not a medical diagnostic tool.
